noah.k: Hey all, quick onboarding hiccup. MDM enrollment succeeded but when I enabled FileVault the flow errored with 'Escrow failed: device not found in KMS'. Asset RWI-1422. What did I break?
it-support: Welcome Noah! Not your fault. Sometimes our KMS lookup lags if the device record hasn't fully propagated. Can you paste output of `sudo fdesetup status` and `profiles status -type enrollment`?
noah.k: `fdesetup: FileVault is Off` and `profiles: Enrolled via MDM (mdm.redwood.internal)`. I did the enable modal and entered my password but the final screen said escrow failed.
it-support: OK — looks like enrollment completed but escrow handshake failed. Two quick fixes: 1) try running `profiles renew -type enrollment` and re-trigger the FileVault enable modal, or 2) we can manually attach the device to the KMS record and then rotate escrow from our side. Trying (1) now?
noah.k: did `profiles renew -type enrollment` and rebooted. Re-ran FileVault enable and it still gave the same escrow failure.
it-support: Thanks. Escalating to security to attach KMS record. Security, can you run a manual link for asset RWI-1422 (serial C02D3ZZZZZ)?
security: On it. I'm seeing a mismatch: the MDM reported serial C02D3ZZZZZ but the KMS record has an old placeholder tag. I'll attach the correct serial to the KMS entry and force a sync. Give me ~2 minutes.
(2 minutes)
security: Done: KMS record updated and sync triggered. Noah, try the FileVault enable flow now.
noah.k: Trying again [0K Modal appeared, went through steps, chose KMS escrow. `sudo fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is On".
it-support: Nice! mdm-bot will record the successful escrow. We'll also add a check to our rollout docs for this propagation edge-case.
mdm-bot: Notice: FileVault escrow completed for asset RWI-1422 at 2026-10-12T09:14:05Z.
inventory-bot: Inventory update: serial C02D3ZZZZZ -> RWI-1422 assigned to noah.k (dev profile applied).
noah.k: Sweet. Able to install Homebrew and set up dotfiles. Thanks for the quick fix :thumbsup:
it-support: Closing out — ping if anything else crops up.
